== Enshrined deities ==
The principal {{ill|Saijin|abstract|Q11591100|fr|Saijin|ja|祭神|zh|祭神|qid=Q11591100}} is {{ill|Ajisukitakahikone|es|Ajisukitakahikone|fr|Ajisukitakahikone|hu|Adzsiszukitakahikone|it|Ajisukitakahikone|ja|アヂスキタカヒコネ|ko|아지스키타카히코네|mni|ꯑꯖꯤꯁꯨꯀꯤꯇꯀꯍꯤꯀꯣꯅꯦ|ru|Адзи-суки-така-хико-нэ|simple|Ajisukitakahikone|zh|味耜高彥根神|qid=Q506610|lt=Ajisukitakahikone-no-Mikoto}} (Kamo no Ōmikami). Associated deities are {{ill|Shitateruhime|fr|Shitateruhime|ja|シタテルヒメ|simple|Shitateru-hime|zh|下照姬|qid=Q11307233|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto}} (daughter of Ōkuninushi), {{ill|Ame no Wakahiko|az|Ame-no-Vakahiko|fr|Ame no Wakahiko|it|Ame no Wakahiko|ja|アメノワカヒコ|ko|아메노와카히코|pl|Młodzian Potrafiący się Oderwać od Nieba|zh|天稚彥|qid=Q10940674|lt=Amenowakahiko-no-Mikoto}} (husband of Shitateruhime), {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|fa|کوتوشیرونوشی|fr|Kotoshironushi|it|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主|ko|고토시로누시|ru|Котосиронуси|simple|Kotoshironushi|th|โคโตชิโรนูชิ|zh|事代主神|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto}}, and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ajisukihayao-no-Mikoto}} (child of the principal deity).

At the sessha Higashi Shrine are enshrined {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|fr|Ama-no-Koyane-no-mikoto|it|Ame-no-Koyane|ja|天児屋命|ko|아메노코야네|mni|ꯑꯃꯦ-ꯅꯣ-ꯀꯣꯌꯅꯦ|pt|Ame-no-Koyane|ru|Амэ-но коянэ-но микото|simple|Ame-no-Koyane|zh|天兒屋命|qid=Q2564508|lt=Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Amaterasu|abstract|Q455602|ar|أماتيراسو|ary|أماطيراسو|az|Amaterasu|bcl|Amaterasu|be|Аматэрасу|be_x_old|Аматэрасу|bew|Amatérasu|bg|Аматерасу|ca|Amaterasu|cs|Amaterasu|da|Amaterasu|de|Amaterasu|el|Αματεράσου|eo|Amaterasu|es|Amaterasu|et|Amaterasu|eu|Amaterasu|fa|آماتراسو|fi|Amaterasu|fr|Amaterasu|gl|Amaterasu|he|אמטראסו|hi|अमातेरसु|hr|Amaterasu|hu|Amateraszu Ómikami|hy|Ամատերասու Օմիկամի|id|Amaterasu|it|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|jv|Amaterasu|ka|ამატერასუ|kk|Аматэрасу|ko|아마테라스 오미카미|la|Amaterasu|lb|Amaterasu|lt|Amaterasu|lv|Amaterasu|mag|अमातेरासु|min|Amaterasu|ml|അമതേരസു|mni|ꯑꯃꯇꯦꯔꯁꯨ ꯑꯣꯃꯤꯀꯃꯤ|ms|Amaterasu|nl|Amaterasu|nn|Amaterasu|no|Amaterasu|or|ଆମାତେରାଶୁ|pa|ਆਮਾਤੇਰਸ|pl|Amaterasu|pt|Amaterasu|ro|Amaterasu|rsk|Аматерасу|ru|Аматэрасу|sco|Amaterasu|sh|Amaterasu|simple|Amaterasu Ōmikami|sk|Amaterasu Ómikami|sl|Amaterasu|sr|Аматерасу|su|Amaterasu|sv|Amaterasu|ta|அமதெரசு|th|อามาเตราซุ|tl|Amaterasu|tok|jan sewi suli Amatelasu|tr|Amaterasu|uk|Аматерасу|uz|Amaterasu|vi|Amaterasu|wuu|天照大神|zh|天照大神|zh_min_nan|Amaterasu|zh_yue|天照大神|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami}}, and {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|de|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|it|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|ja|住吉三神|mni|ꯁꯨꯃꯤꯌꯣꯁꯤ ꯁꯟꯖꯤꯟ|my|ဆုမိရောရှိနတ်သုံးပါး|pl|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|simple|Sumiyoshi sanjin|zh|住吉三神|qid=Q1114013|lt=Sumiyoshi Sanzen Ōkami}}. At the sessha Nishi Shrine are enshrined {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tagirihime-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ame-no-Mikatsuhime-no-Mikoto}} (consort of the principal deity), {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shionihiko-no-Mikoto}} (child), and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Takitsuhiko-no-Mikoto}} (child).

It is thought that originally only Ajisukitakahikone and Shitateruhime were enshrined, and later, under influence of mythology, Amenowakahiko (as Shitateruhime's husband) and Tagirihime (as mother) were added. However, there are many differing theories on deities other than the principal one. '{{ill|Tokusen Jinmyōchō|ja|特選神名牒|qid=Q11571092}}' gives Ajisukitakahikone and Tagirihime; another theory says deities other than the principal are unknown.

== Origin ==
This area is the birthplace of the {{ill|Kamo no Ason clan|ja|賀茂朝臣氏|qid=Q122979457|lt=Kamo clan}} and this shrine was enshrined as their {{ill|Ujigami|de|Ujigami|es|Ujigami|fa|اوجی‌گامی|fr|Ujigami|ja|氏神|ko|씨신|mni|ꯎꯖꯤꯒꯃꯤ|pl|Ujigami|ro|Ujigami|simple|Ujigami|te|ఉజిగామి|uk|Удзіґамі|zh|氏神|qid=Q767655}}. Branches of the clan moved from these hills into the {{ill|Nara Basin|ja|奈良盆地|ko|나라 분지|ru|Ямато (равнина)|zh|奈良盆地|qid=Q10942269}}: a branch that moved to the bank of the {{ill|Katsuragi River|ceb|Katsuragi Gawa|ja|葛城川|qid=Q11620895}} enshrined {{ill|Kamo Tsuba Shrine|ja|鴨都波神社|qid=Q11675614}}, and one that moved to Higashi-Mochida enshrined {{ill|Katsuragi Mitoshi Shrine|ja|葛木御歳神社|qid=Q11620955}}. Later, Takakamo Shrine came to be called Kami-Kamo-sha, Mitoshi Shrine Naka-Kamo-sha, and Kamotsuba Shrine Shimo-Kamo-sha.

In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}, it is listed as "Takakamo Ajisukitakihikone-no-Mikoto Shrine, four seats," ranked myojin-taisha, and noted as receiving offerings at monthly, aidame, and niiname rites.
